1	/* Wren's design system, version 1: the tokens.
2	
3	   The design system belongs to neither a hub nor a groove. A hub themes it; a
4	   groove is built against it and says so, by linking this version. What
5	   crosses between them is here - colour, type, space, shape and depth, each
6	   named for what it is *for* rather than what it looks like - and nothing else.
7	
8	   The cascade, lowest first, declared once so every file agrees:
9	
10	     tokens      these defaults
11	     base        elements - the page, links, headings, form controls
12	     components  .card, .btn, .field and the rest, in components.css
13	     host        a hub's own chrome, and its own token values if it has any
14	
15	   and, above every layer, whatever a groove writes itself. That last part is
16	   the point of layers: a groove's plain `.metronome input` beats a hub's
17	   `input:not([type=hidden]):not(...)` without matching its specificity, or
18	   knowing it exists. A layer is a statement about who wins; specificity is an
19	   accident of how somebody else wrote their selector.
20	
21	   These values sit in the lowest layer so that they are defaults, not
22	   decisions. A hub that wants its own accent writes `--accent` anywhere else
23	   and wins; a hub that writes nothing still gets a palette that works; and a
24	   groove on a bare page, with no hub around it at all, renders as it should.
25	
26	   Colours are OKLCH, each written once with light-dark(), so one definition
27	   serves both themes. Which theme applies is `color-scheme`, which is the
28	   host's to set: the page belongs to the host, so the host decides how it
29	   looks, and a groove never asks. */
30	
31	@layer tokens, base, components, host;
32	
33	@layer tokens {
34	  :root {
35	    color-scheme: light dark;
36	
37	    /* Surfaces, from the page back to the most raised */
38	    --bg:             light-dark(oklch(0.982 0.004 75), oklch(0.165 0.006 60));
39	    --surface:        light-dark(oklch(1 0 0),

text:
1	# Prelude
2	
3	A tool for designing (and later building) apps with an agent: pick a folder,
4	chat with an agent, watch the design appear. The plan, its ground rules and
5	every decision taken are in `docs/plan.md`. Read it before adding a feature.
6	Nothing gets added until we've decided where it fits in the simple model
7	(folder, design, session, screen; a chat surface and a design surface).
8	
9	## Koda
10	
11	This application is built with Koda. Before writing or changing a view, a
12	stylesheet or a handler, load the matching skill - `koda-app-authoring`,
13	`koda-styling`, `koda-server-setup` (and `koda-composition` for anything that
14	crosses an application or a host) - and follow it. Look attributes up in the
15	Koda reference (`node_modules/@kodalang/core/docs/reference.md`, the version
16	Prelude depends on) rather than from memory. Run `koda-review` before calling a
17	change finished.
18	
19	Koda is the npm package `@kodalang/core`, pinned in `package.json`, and it ships
20	its skills. The ones in `.claude/skills/` are copies of the installed package's;
21	`test/skills.test.js` fails when they differ. After upgrading Koda, run
22	`npm run skills` to copy them again, and read what changed.
23	
24	## Working here
25	
26	- `npm start` runs Prelude on http://localhost:4200 (`PORT` to change it).
27	  Views are cached when the server starts: restart it after changing one.
28	- `npm test` runs the tests (node --test). Add tests for what you build.
29	- The desktop app: `npm run build:shell` builds `tauri/src-tauri` (about 10
30	  minutes from cold) into `dist-shell/Prelude.exe`. `npm run test:shell` runs its
31	  Rust tests. The app is a window on the server: it uses one already answering
32	  `/health` on localhost:4200 (`npm start`), or else starts `node start.js`
33	  itself (Prelude's folder is found above the exe, or `--root`/`PRELUDE_ROOT`;
34	  its output goes to `~/.prelude/server.log`) and stops it on quit. `--server
35	  <url>` or `PRELUDE_URL` p

text:
I've built Prelude's design system from what Prelude already ships: the `ds/v1` tokens, components and icons, plus the patterns in `prelude.css` and the views. It's in `prelude/prelude-design-system/`. The gallery has three screens: Tokens, Components and Guidelines. Each has a System/Light/Dark switch at the top so you can look at both themes. I haven't opened it in a browser, so it needs your eye in the preview.

**Kept as it was:** the look. The warm neutrals, sienna accent, type scale, 4px spacing, corner radii and shadows are all the same, and each token is still named for its role.

**What I changed:**
- **Prelude's own patterns are now components.** That's the list rows, menus, Design/App switch (now "segmented"), design bar (now "toolbar"), panels, notices, the agent's status line, transcript, message box, rendered markdown (now "prose"), empty states, crumbs, expandable "more" sections and radio/checkbox choices. The page layout itself is left out, because that belongs to the app shell.
- **Smaller buttons by default.** In `ds/v1` the standard button was 3.25rem tall and primary buttons were 4rem, so Prelude used `.small` or a local height override everywhere. Now a button is 2.5rem, the same height as an input, so a field and its button line up. `.small` is 2rem for toolbars and `.large` is 3.25rem. Primary changes the colour, not the size.
- **One clear name per thing.** For example, `.f` → `.label`, `.err` → `.error`, `.rowbtns` → `.actions`, and the two icon-button classes are now one, `.icon-btn`. The full list is in `NOTES.md`. I also added `.hint`, `.pill.warn` and `.pill.accent`.
- **No literal sizes in components.** New tokens cover control heights, the dialog backdrop, border width and motion; motion drops to zero under reduced motion. Ghost buttons no longer have a border, which makes the toolbars quieter.
- **Warning colour darkened slightly** in light mode, so warning text reads clearly on white.
- **Icons:** 32 of the `ds/v1` icons, chosen for what Prelude needs. `conversation` is now `session` and `activity` is now `history`. Pop out should use `external` rather than `expand`, which means "show more below".
- **Guidelines:** 10 rules, each with its reason and a do and don't. There's also a word list of Prelude's terms and the ones to avoid, such as session rather than chat, and "Not now" rather than "Cancel".

**Open questions, also in `NOTES.md`:**
1. Should Prelude's own app move onto this system and replace `ds/v1` + `prelude.css`? The views would need a pass for the renamed classes.
2. The set has no icon for pop out or for copy.
3. Do we need the dialog at all? Prelude asks for confirmation in the page today.
Committed to prelude/prelude-design-system (69ad8dd).

I was enhancing Prelude's support for layout primitives in its components and we ended up with the following prompt. Let's add these to our design system.

Layout primitives. Besides its components, the system provides layout primitives: classes that arrange their children and own the space between them. Pages are composed from them, so spacing is consistent everywhere.
- Each primitive spaces its children with gap, using only the system's spacing tokens (--space-*), never margins on the children. Offer a way to choose the gap from that scale (a modifier class, or a custom property set from a token).
- Each copes with narrow widths without @media: by wrapping, by auto-fill, by flex-basis, or by a container query.
- Choose the set the product needs, and name each one for what it does. Common ones, to take, rename or leave out: stack (children one under another); cluster (a row that wraps: toolbars, tags, label-and-value pairs); grid (equal columns that fill the width, as many as fit); split (a main part and a side part, the side dropping below when narrow); center (content held to a readable width). If the app already has layout helpers, use those, under the app's names.
- Each is a component like any other: in components.css (@layer components), with its canonical markup in components/, shown on the gallery's components screen.
- Add a rule to guidelines.md saying how pages are composed: blocks sit inside primitives, and the space between blocks comes only from their gaps.
If system/ has no layout primitives yet, add them this turn.

I've added five layout primitives to the design system, plus a guideline on how pages are composed from them. I haven't viewed any of it in a browser, so check the gallery in the preview. **The primitives**, in `components.css`, each with a file in `components/`: - **`.stack`**: children one under another. A page, a form, or a label with its list. The default gap is `--space-4`. - **`.cluster`**: a row that wraps, for buttons, pills, or a label and its value. The default gap is `--space-2`. `.baseline` lines text up on its baseline, and `.end` pushes everything to the end. - **`.grid`**: equal columns, as many as fit. Each is at least `--min` wide (14rem unless you set it). - **`.split`**: a main part beside a `.side` part. The side wraps onto its own line once the main part would drop below 55% of the row. Prelude's chat beside its design is one of these. - **`.center`**: content held to a readable width, with a gutter. `.narrow` makes it narrower. You set the gap with `.gap-0` … `.gap-10`, or with `style="--gap: var(--space-…)"`. Each primitive sets its own default, so a nested one doesn't pick up its parent's gap. None uses `@media`; they cope with narrow widths by wrapping, auto-fill or flex-basis. Prelude had no general layout helpers to reuse. `.page` belongs to the app shell, and `.inline` and `.fields` are form-specific, so those two stay as form components. The primitives therefore use the common names. **What changed so the space comes only from gaps:** - Headings, paragraphs, lists, cards, notices, crumbs, choices and `.actions` no longer have outer margins. Cards, fields, notices and the message box now space their own parts with gap. - A row of buttons is now written `class="cluster actions"`. - A notice's text has to go in a `

`. Without one, inline code inside a notice would break up the line. - Rendered markdown (`.prose`) is the one exception and still spaces itself. **Guidelines:** a new rule 8 says every block sits inside a primitive and the space between blocks comes only from their gaps. Rule 7 now says the page's frame belongs to the app shell and what's inside it is built from primitives. **Gallery:** the Components screen opens with a new Layout section. The cluster, grid and split examples can be resized by dragging a corner, so you can watch them wrap. All three gallery screens are now built from the primitives themselves. Their own stylesheet has no margins left. `NOTES.md` records these decisions.
